svg.text: USB Power Distribution — Smart Airport Baggage Management System
one USB cable powers everything · the Black Pill supplies BOTH rails, so no separate power module is needed
POWER ONLY. For signal wiring (sensor AO, UART, buzzer base, button) see wiring-diagram.svg
Both TCRT5000 sensors go on the 3.3 V rail — never 5 V. PA1 / PA4 are analog inputs and are NOT 5 V tolerant.
A 5 V phone charger or a USB
only the pins used in this drawing are labelled
one jumper ties the two − rails
the 5V jumper runs round the left end of the board
5 V buzzer, BC547, 1 k base R
the two sensors sit in the belt deck — what plugs into the board here are their flying leads
1. Lay the two + rails and the two − rails first.
2. Plug in the Black Pill, straddling the channel.
3. Run three jumpers: 3V3 → bottom +, 5V → top +, G → bottom −.
4. Tie the two − rails together with one more jumper.
5. Plug in USB. PC13 should blink once a second.
6. Measure both rails with a multimeter BEFORE adding anything
else. You want 3.3 V and 5.0 V. If either is wrong, stop.
7. Only then add the HC-05, the buzzer and the sensors.
A laptop USB 2.0 port supplies 500 mA, so there is
roughly four times the headroom needed.
Use red, orange and black jumpers to match.

Do not power the ST-LINK rail at the same time
Once USB is plugged in, connect only THREE ST-LINK wires:
SWDIO→PA13, SWCLK→PA14, GND→GND. Leave its 3.3 V
wire off. Two regulators driving the same rail is how you
Why there is no MB102 in this drawing
The Black Pill already contains the 3.3 V regulator, and its
5V pin passes USB VBUS straight through. A second supply
Buy an MB102 only if you want the rig to run with no USB
cable attached at all. The guide covers that variant.
The HC-05 needs 3.6 V minimum, so it must come off the 5 V
rail and never the 3.3 V one: its onboard regulator cannot
work with only 3.3 V going in.
